reason: The preserved native Text inventory contract rejects pages with non-text paint because glyph evidence cannot classify text in images or paths. At least one side of 35 fixed pairs has such paint. The sole remaining pair failed both acquisition probes. Even granting that pair completion gives only one pair, fewer than the required two. Existing renderers do not establish recognized text; OCR and semantic models are prohibited. Ignoring paint, replacing panel pairs, or counting opaque paint as recognized text would change the fixed contract or denominator.
scope_of_conclusion: This is a constraint of this fixed panel, preserved inventory contract and permitted acquisition routes, not a claim that no future non-OCR proof system could ever compare these documents. Such a proof system and its Text inventory contract would require a revised completion contract before this gate could be claimed.
